title: Fidelity multiplexing capacity plan (Jun 2029)
body:
Purpose:
This worksheet synthesizes recent multiplexing experiments with mixed-precision profiles to produce a near-term regional GPU capacity plan. Focus is on mapping throughput uplift against expected fidelity loss (relative QA delta) and producing actionable reserve recommendations for NA / EU / APAC for Q3–Q4 2029.

Summary conclusions (high level):
- Adaptive multiplexing (soft-concurrency + dynamic micro-batches) + 8-bit kernel yields up to ~2.6x aggregate token throughput vs baseline FP16 static batching for conversational load, with median quality delta estimated at -1.8% (small but measurable; affects long-tail completion quality).
- Aggressive 4-bit schemes unlock additional capacity (3.5x vs FP16) but show non-linear quality degradation on long contexts and retrieval-heavy prompts (~-6% quality delta on eval set).
- Recommended conservative rollout: enable 8-bit multiplexing fleet-wide with per-route canaries; provision a 10% dedicated FP16 headroom in each region for sensitive customers / eval rollbacks.

Assumptions and definitions:
- Baseline: FP16 kernel, static batch size tuned per model family, single-request concurrency 1.
- Multiplexing: runtime-level request interleaving with micro-batches (micro-batch size 4–16 tokens), soft-priority scheduling for low-latency routes.
- Throughput uplift measured as tokens/sec per GPU under representative mixed workload (50% short chat, 30% medium instruct, 20% longcontext).
- Quality metric: composite score (normalized) combining LM log-prob regression on held-out generation set + task-specific evals; reported as relative % delta vs baseline (negative -> worse).

Regional projection table (conservative forecast):
Region | Current GPUs | Baseline tokens/s/GPU | 8-bit multiplex tokens/s/GPU | 4-bit multiplex tokens/s/GPU | Est. 8-bit quality delta | Est. 4-bit quality delta | Recommended reserve GPUs
NA     | 280          | 2,400                 | 6,100                        | 8,500                        | -1.7%                   | -5.8%                   | 28
EU     | 160          | 2,300                 | 5,900                        | 8,100                        | -1.9%                   | -6.2%                   | 16
APAC   | 90           | 2,200                 | 5,400                        | 7,900                        | -2.4%                   | -7.1%                   | 9

Notes on table entries:
- Current GPUs are active, serving-capable GPUs (not including hot spares).
- Baseline tokens/s/GPU are median observed across model families (Llama-deriv & open-weights) on production input mix.
- Throughput numbers for 8-bit/4-bit are median of 10 stress runs with 95th percentile tails trimmed. Variance increases in APAC due to heavier long-context share.

Operational policy recommendations:
1) Canary plan (2–3 week window):
   - Phase 1 (week 1): Enable 8-bit multiplexing for non-SLA routes (internal dev, free-tier) in NA only. Monitor token quality regression and user-visible error rates.
   - Phase 2 (weeks 2–3): Expand 8-bit to EU and APAC with per-region gate and enable response-quality alerts tied to key prompt sets.
   - Phase 3 (post-canary): Consider selective 4-bit for high-throughput but low-criticality workloads (embeddings-only, non-customer-facing batch transforms).

2) Headroom and failover:
   - Keep ~10% of active fleet as FP16-only pool in each region for instant rollback and sensitive customer routing.
   - Configure routing policy to fall back to FP16 in <250ms route saturation events or when quality-alert thresholds cross.

3) Monitoring & evals:
   - Add per-route quality delta charts (weekly) feeding into rollout automation.
   - Expand eval set to include retrieval+long-context prompts (these drive worst-case 4-bit regression).

Open questions / risks:
- Long-tail latency spikes: multiplexing increases inter-request jitter; need to validate p99 latency SLA impact across 24-hour windows.
- Model-specific sensitivity: some weights exhibit outsized quality loss under 4-bit; model-variant tagging required in catalog.
- Measurement noise: small relative quality deltas (~1–2%) may be within sampling noise for some routes — need larger eval sample or synthetic adversarial prompts.

Experiment log (abridged):
- EXP-786 (May 2029): 8-bit multiplexing + soft-priority scheduler; NA pilot 48 GPUs; result: +2.5x mean throughput, median quality -1.6%.
- EXP-804 (Jun 2029): 4-bit mixed scheme with activation-aware calibration; EU pilot 32 GPUs; result: +3.3x mean throughput, median quality -5.9%, 95th-tail quality loss up to -12% on retrieval prompts.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- [Ravi] finalize canary rollout playbook and rollback hooks (ETA: 2029-06-21).
- [Maya] add long-context evaluation set and integrate into alerting (ETA: 2029-06-28).
- [Liam] prepare routing fallback rules and test cross-region failover (ETA: 2029-07-05).
- [SRE] reserve recommended GPUs as warm hot-spares and validate provisioning scripts (ETA: 2029-07-10).

Appendix: quick sensitivity sampler (notes)
- Small increase in micro-batch size gave diminishing returns after size 12 and increased p99 latency by ~8%.
- Dynamic kv-cache reuse during multiplexing critical to keep quality delta within 2% for 8-bit runs.
- For embeddings workloads, 4-bit quant yields >4x throughput with negligible quality impact; isolate via route classification.

Comments/notes to self:
- Keep this sheet as living doc; update with per-route empirical deltas as canary progresses.
- Cross-ref INFRA-8342 for GPU procurement lead times and CONFLUENCE-1219 for rollout runbook.
